title: Sheesha
tagline: Ek ghar. Ek rule. Tees raatein.
disclosure_line: यह एक काल्पनिक कहानी है। इस चैनल की सारी फुटेज और आवाज़ AI से बनाई गई है।
logline: A man inherits his grandfather's house in a small North-Indian town with one rule: at night, do not look at yourself in the mirror. It sees you first.

rule.text_hinglish: Raat ko sheeshe mein apna chehra mat dekho. Woh pehle tumhe dekh leta hai.
rule.text_devanagari: रात को शीशे में अपना चेहरा मत देखो। वो पहले तुम्हें देख लेता है।
rule.origin: Written by Nana, handed over with the house keys in a courier's envelope.
rule.cost_mechanic: The mirror keeps a copy. Each night inside the 30-minute window it takes one more detail of the narrator's face. When it holds every detail, it steps out and the original is left inside.
rule.countdown: Thirty nights. One episode per night. The season ends when the copy is complete.

setting.place: An inherited old house in a small North-Indian town
anchor_locations: hall mirror, draped in an old sari
stairwell with a fourth step that creaks
the dry well behind the kitchen
kitchen with a wall clock stopped at 2:30
hard_world_rules: There is no second mirror in the house.
There is no electricity after 2 AM.
The well is dry and has been for years.
The house was never sold; it was inherited. No purchase money, only the keys.
The clock in the kitchen is stuck at 2:30 and does not move forward.

cast.name: main
cast.arc: refuses the rule, then weaponises it, then pays for it

cast.name: nana
cast.on_screen: cane silhouette, seen only in recordings or a doorway
cast.arc: the only one who knew the rule and never told his son

cast.name: maa
cast.arc: has kept the mirror covered for twenty years and has her own debt at the mirror

cast.name: papa
cast.role: father, works in the Gulf, phone calls only
cast.arc: knew something, and his warning arrives too late

cast.name: the one on the other side
cast.arc: no motivation, no bargain, only a checklist of details to finish

cast.name: Babulal
cast.on_screen: never speaks - exists only as a written note
cast.arc: his note is the third of three keys to the ending

motifs.desc: the covered hall mirror - the threat and the clock
jasmine, cut and wet on the morning after each night
three knocks from the courtyard, never four
Nana's kurta on a hanger, warm
Nana's cassette carrying the narrator's own voice

forbidden_states: The narrator is never named on screen or in narration.
No character is ever given a visible, detailed face. Silhouette and backlight only.
The mirror is never broken. It cannot be broken - only covered, or traded with.
The Presence never explains itself, never bargains, never is defeated by an argument.
Papa never physically appears in the house.
No second mirror is ever introduced.
No episode may resolve the season-long question before episode 29.
No gore, no blood, no weapons, no real persons, no real place names.

arcs.name: Pehli Raat
arcs.goal: establish the rule, the house, and the first six stolen details

arcs.name: Khoja
arcs.goal: investigate Nana's notes; discover the copy is three days ahead and that Maa is also in debt

arcs.name: Aakhri
arcs.goal: the Presence steps out; the narrator breaks the rule on purpose and swaps places

continuity_rules: Nights run in order; episode N is night N.
Stolen details are cumulative and never regress: posture (ep4), clothes (ep3), age (ep5), spectacles (ep11), mother's voice (ep19).
The copy is always exactly three days ahead of the narrator once episode 18 reveals it.
Maa's twenty-year cover only comes off the mirror in episode 16.
Every episode ends on a cliffhanger that the next episode opens by resolving.
